Finding: OSD-569 CBC transformed hemoglobin header says percent
Evidence: Submitted CBC uses g/dL for matching subject/timepoint values
Required handling: Preserve both files. Quarantine unit mapping until reviewed. Do not convert percentages into g/dL

Finding: Most Inspiration4 phenotyping concerns four people on a three-day LEO mission
Evidence: Individual assays and timepoints have smaller/different coverage
Required handling: Record cohort and assay-level sample counts. Do not claim long-duration predictive validation

Finding: OSD-687 histone study describes one crew member at R+194
Evidence: Mission-level crew count is not assay cohort count
Required handling: Keep participant count at study/assay level; do not label all I4 tables n=4

Finding: Human-tagged query returns human-derived cell and mixed-organism studies too
Evidence: Species tag does not prove a crew cohort
Required handling: Triage metadata before selecting training or validation samples

Finding: RadLab GUI documentation download returned HTTP 500 during collection
Required handling: Keep successful historical snapshot and failed-attempt log; do not infer live reliability

Finding: Absorbed dose, dose equivalent, effective dose and flux differ
Evidence: APIs expose different units and physical meanings
Required handling: No implicit conversion to the NASA career effective-dose limit

Finding: BIDMC contains critically ill Earth patients
Evidence: It is not a healthy astronaut reference population
Required handling: Use for ingestion, timestamp and waveform tests only

Finding: Sleep-EDF telemetry study includes placebo/temazepam conditions
Evidence: A PSG sample is not astronaut actigraphy
Required handling: Retain condition dictionary and annotation method; avoid clinical generalization

Finding: No public live NASA crew medical-device API established
Evidence: Research download APIs differ from onboard acquisition
Required handling: Require an actual sample export or SDK before claiming integration

Finding: Lab reference ranges and NASA requirements have different applicability
Evidence: Assay method, specimen, individual baseline and time window matter
Required handling: Medical reviewer must approve any rule and action before a clinical claim

Finding: Sources use mission-relative L-/R+/FD time and ordinary timestamps
Evidence: A relative time label is not a UTC instant
Required handling: Preserve raw time, anchor, uncertainty and ingestion time separately

Finding: Public processed results coexist with controlled raw human data
Evidence: Access is checked at file level
Required handling: Do not request, infer or redistribute controlled data; no reidentification
